speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you've provided your symptoms: fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To narrow this down, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; given your weight loss and night sweats, have you noticed any fevers or specific pain when you swallow or lift your arm? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, and ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC - Elevated, Hemoglobin - Slightly Decreased, Platelets - Normal; Lactate_Dehydrogenase - Elevated; ESR - Not Provided in Data

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated WBC and LDH combined with your symptoms are highly suggestive of a lymphoma. Can you tell me if you have noticed any lumps or swelling in your neck, armpits, or groin, and do you experience itching after a warm shower or bath? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray and Neck_Scanner.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), elevated LDH, supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and the specific description of the neck node as "fixed" strongly supports this diagnosis. Please proceed with a biopsy of the supraclavicular node for confirmation.
